title: CLR/160/2016 of DINESH CHANDRA JAISWAL Vs SUBHASH CHANDRA

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT NAINITAL
 Civil Revision No.160 of 2016
Dinesh Chandra Jaiswal Ö.Revisionist
 Vs.
Subhash Chandra ...Respondent
Present:
Mr. Sarvesh Agarwal, Advocate for the revisionist
Mr. P.C. Maulekhi, Advocate for the respondent
Honíble Lok Pal Singh, J.
Instant civil revision, preferred under Section 25
of the Provincial Small Causes Court Act, is directed
against the judgment and decree dated 20.10.2016 passed
by Additional District Judge, Ramnagar, District Nainital
in S.C.C. Suit No.17 of 2015, whereby the suit of the
plaintiff/revisionist for a decree of ejectment and arrears
of rent/damages has been dismissed.
2. Factual matrix of the case is that the
revisionist/plaintiff instituted a suit being SCC suit no.17
of 2015 against the respondent/defendant in the court of
Judge, SCC/District Judge, Nainital for a decree of
ejectment, arrears of rent and mesne profit, stating that
the revisionist/plaintiff is owner and landlord of the shop
in dispute. The respondent/defendant is tenant in the said
shop at the rent of ` 833.33/-. He has committed default
in payment of rent since 01.04.2009 wherefor a registered
notice dated 30.11.2014 was sent by the
revisionist/plaintiff to the respondent/defendant
terminating his tenancy. The notice was duly served upon
the respondent on 04.12.2014 but despite this neither the
respondent deposited the arrears of rent, nor he vacated

2
the shop in dispute. The respondent/defendant contested
the suit and filed his written statement stating therein
that his father was inducted as tenant in the shop in
dispute, and after his death, he is under the tenancy of
the plaintiff. He further stated that he is regularly paying
the rent of the tenanted shop. In the year 2012, when he
demanded rent receipt from the plaintiff, the plaintiff
refused to give the same, due to which the defendant
constrained to file the rent control case no.13 of 2012
under Section 30(1) of The U.P. Urban Buildings
(Regulation of Letting, Rent and Eviction) Act, 1972
(hereinafter to be referred as the U.P. Act No.13 of 1972)
and as per the order dated 17.05.2012 he deposited two
yearsí rent in the court on 29.05.2012 vide challan no.6
and thereafter on 07.08.2014 he deposited the entire rent
for the year 2014. The defendant further stated that he
has deposited the entire rent in the court on the first date
of hearing of the suit.
3. On the pleadings of parties, learned Judge, SCC
framed the following points of determination:-
(i) Whether the defendant is tenant in the shop in
question @ ` 833.33/- per month? If yes, its effect.
(ii) Whether the defendant has committed default in
payment of rent w.e.f. 01.04.2009?
(iii) Whether the notice dated 30.11.2014 sent by the
plaintiff to the respondent is valid and legal?
(iv) Whether the plaintiff is entitled to receive
`31,395/- towards arrears of rent and mesne
profit @ ` 27.80 per day along with interest @ 9 %
per annum from the defendant?
(v) To what relief the plaintiff is entitled for?

3
4. Thereafter, the parties led their oral as well as
documentary evidence. In documentary evidence, the
plaintiff filed carbon copy of notice dated 30.11.2014,
original copy of postal receipt, acknowledgment, etc. In
oral evidence, plaintiff Dinesh Chandra Jaiswal got
examined himself as PW1. On the other hand, the
defendant filed challan form vide list no.16C/1 to 16C/2,
original copies of rent receipt, order dated 17.05.2012
passed in rent control case no.13/2012, photocopies of
challan form vide which the defendant deposited the rent,
application paper no.27C/8 moved by the defendant for
depositing the rent, paper no.27C/9 notice information,
etc. In oral evidence, the defendant got examined himself
as DW1.
5. After hearing the learned counsel for the parties
and on perusal of entire evidence on record, learned Judge
SCC on issue no.1 recorded a finding that the landlord-tenant relationship is admitted to the parties and the
provisions of U.P. Act No.13 of 1972 are applicable to the
shop in question. A further finding was recorded that the
plaintiff has pleaded that the shop in question was under
the tenancy of the defendant @ ` 833.33/- per month
whereas the defendant has pleaded that it was an annual
tenancy and the rate of rent was ` 10,000/- including
taxes but as neither any rent deed nor any written
agreement was produced by either party, the tribunal held
that it is proved that the defendant was under the annual
tenancy @ Rs.10,000/- per annum.
6. On issue no.2, learned Judge recorded a finding
that the defendant has filed documentary evidence to
show that he has deposited the rent amounting to `
30,000/- for the year 2012 to 2014 in the competent court

4
under Section 30 of the U.P. Act No.13 of 1972 and
thereafter has also deposited the balance rent amounting
to ` 40,000/- on 26.05.2015 by the orders of this court,
and in this regard, intimation was sent to the plaintiff by
the court. The trial court on the point as to whether the
defendant is entitled to get protection under Section 20(4)
of the U.P. Act No.13 of 1972, recorded finding that the
plaintiff instituted the suit on 30.04.2015 which was
presented before the Judge, SCC on 01.05.2015, on which
date, the Judge SCC issued notices to the defendant for
filing written statement and fixed the date for 26.06.2015.
As such, the first date of hearing in the suit was
26.05.2015. The trial court recorded finding that before
the first date of hearing the defendant deposited the
balance amount of rent to the tune of ` 40,000/- in the
court and has also deposited ` 30,000/- towards rent
under Section 30 of the U.P. Act No.13 of 1972. It was
thus held that the defendant has deposited the amount
more than the amount claimed by the plaintiff, in
accordance with law. As such, the trial court recorded
finding that the defendant is entitled to get the benefit of
Section 20(4) of the U.P. Act No.13 of 1972.
7. On issue nos.3 and 4, learned Judge SCC
recorded finding that as it has been held in issue no.2 that
the tenancy of the defendant is protected in view of
provisions of Section 20(4) of U.P. Act No.13 of 1972,
hence, the defendant is not liable to be evicted on the
basis of notice dated 30.11.2014. On issue no.5, learned
Judge SCC held that in view of the findings recorded in
issue nos.1 to 4, the suit of the plaintiff is liable to be
dismissed. Accordingly, by judgment and order dated
20.10.2016, learned Judge SCC, dismissed the suit of the
plaintiff.

5
8. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and
perused the entire material on record.
9. Learned counsel for the revisionist would
submit that the learned Judge, SCC has recorded a
perverse finding to the effect that the defendant is entitled
to get the benefit of Section 20(4) of U.P. Act No.13 of
1972. He would further submit that the amount deposited
by the defendant under the said Act was insufficient.
10. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent
would submit that the defendant has deposited the entire
amount of rent on the first date of hearing of the suit and
the court below has rightly granted benefit to the
defendant as provided under the said section.
11. Having considered the rival submissions of the
parties, the core issue which arises for consideration of
this Court is as to whether the tenancy of the defendant is
protected in view of provisions contained in sub-section (4)
of Section 20 of U.P. Act No.13 of 1972, as has been
observed by the trial court.
12. Before any discussion, it would be apt to
discuss sub-section (4) of Section 20 of the U.P. Act No.13
of 1972, which is reproduced hereunder:-
ì20. Bar of suit for eviction of tenant except on specified
grounds.
Ö
(4) In any suit for eviction on the ground mentioned in
clause (a) of sub-section (2), if at the first hearing of the
suit the tenant unconditionally pays or [tenders to the
landlord or deposits in Court] the entire amount of rent
and damages for use and calculated at the same rate as

6
rent) together with interest thereon at the rate of nine per
cent per annum and the landlordís costs of the suit in
respect thereof, after deducting therefrom any amount
already deposited by the tenant under sub-section (1) of
Section 30, the Court may, in lieu of passing a decree for
eviction on that ground, pass an order reliving the tenant
against his liability for eviction on that ground :
Provided that nothing in this sub-section shall apply in
relation to a tenant who or any member of whose family
has built or has otherwise acquired in a vacant state, or
has got vacated after acquisition, any residential building
in the same city, municipality, notified area or town area.
[Explanation.-For the purposes of this sub-section-
(a) the expression ëfirst hearingí means the first date
for any step or proceeding mentioned in the
summons served on the defendant ;
(b) the expression ëcost of the suití includes one-half of
the amount of counselís fee taxable for a contested
suit].î
13. A plain language of the aforesaid provision
makes it clear that in a suit for eviction if on the first date
of hearing, the tenant unconditionally pays or deposits the
entire rent in the court or tenders it to the landlord, as the
case may be, along with damages for use and the interest
@ 9% per annum thereon as well as the landlordís costs of
the suit, he/she would be entitled to be relieved from a
decree of eviction. The expression ëfirst date of hearingí is
explained as the first date for any step or for any step or
proceeding mentioned in the summons served on the
defendant.
14. In the case at hand, there is no dispute with
regard to the first date of hearing. Suit was instituted by
the plaintiff on 30.04.2015, whereafter on 01.05.2015 the

7
suit was registered and the notices were issued to the
defendant to file written statement and the date was fixed
for 26.06.2015. Thus, the first date of hearing in the
present suit is 26.06.2015 for which date summons were
issued to the defendant. Now it is to be as to whether the
defendant had deposited the entire rent along with
damages, costs of the suit and the interest thereon, on the
first date of hearing i.e. 26.06.2015.
15. A perusal of the plaint would reveal that the
plaintiff pleaded that the defendant has committed default
in making payment of the rent of the shop in dispute since
01.04.2009, and accordingly he claimed rent to the tune
of ` 57,555/- for the period 01.04.2009 to 02.01.2015
along with damages @ ` 27.80/- per day (in total
Rs.3280/-) and notice expenses ` 1100/-, for the period
03.01.2015 to 30.04.2015. In all, he pleaded that the rent
amounting to ` 61,905/- is due upon the respondent,
however, as the rent due for the period 01.09.2009 to
31.03.2012 was time-barred, the plaintiff claimed rent
amounting to ` 31,935/- only. In this regard, the
defendant averred in the written statement and in the oral
testimony that he deposited the entire amount of rent `
31,935/-, court fees ` 2807.50/-, interest @ 9% ` 1157.50
and counsel fee Rs.1100/-, in total ` 40,000/- on the first
date of hearing. He also filed treasury challan paper
no.16C/2 to substantiate his claim. Besides this, the
defendant also deposited two yearsí rent for the year 2012
and 2013 and further an amount of ` 10,000/- for the
year 2014 before the competent court under Section 30 of
the U.P. Act No.13 of 1972.
16. In view of the above, it is ample clear that the
defendant has deposited the entire amount of rent as

8
claimed by the plaintiff, along with damages, cost of suit
and interest @ 9%, on the first date of hearing. That being
the position, learned Judge SCC has rightly extended the
benefit of the provisions of sub-section (4) of Section 20 of
the U.P. Act no.13 of 1972 in favour of the
respondent/defendant, thereby protecting the tenancy of
the respondent/defendant. There is no illegality or
irregularity in the judgment and order passed by the court
below.
17. Accordingly, there is no merit in the instant civil
revision. Same is hereby dismissed.
 (Lok Pal Singh, J.)
 24.11.2020
